summary: TrendDetect is a system capable of analyzing meteorological data from NASA's Power API. Its dual output system lets it analyze both time series and location data. You can analyze how meteorological data trends over time, as well as how locations in an area can experience different data trends. I used regression to analyze time series as well as the Mann Kendall Test to ensure data isn't due to random fluctuations.
details:
TrendDetect uses a dual system to analyze trends in meteorological data of the Earth. To make it work, I used two data representations: location and time.

Time

For the time representation, I plotted the data that the user requests on the Y axis and the time in years on the X axis. I then used the Mann Kendall test to identify trends such as S, Z, etc. Finally I allowed 3 types of regression, those begin linear, quadratic and cubic.

Location

For the location representation, I plotted the data on a 3D surface of the earth we live on. Every point represented a data sample. This way, the user can look at the overall surface of the earth and how data changes over this field.
